simple_definition: Required by law or rule; compulsory.
detailed_definition: Required by law or a set of rules; obligatory, not optional.
examples: Wearing a seatbelt is mandatory in most countries.
Attendance at the training session is mandatory for all staff.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about government policy and education rules.

simple_definition: Required by law or a rule; must be done.
detailed_definition: Required by law or a rule; obligatory.
examples: Compulsory education continues until the age of sixteen in many countries.
Some argue that military service should be compulsory for young adults.
ielts_relevance: Common Task 2 topic word, especially education essays.

simple_definition: Done or given willingly, without being forced or paid.
detailed_definition: Done, given, or acting of one's own free will, without being paid or forced.
examples: She spends her weekends doing voluntary work at a local shelter.
Participation in the survey is entirely voluntary.
ielts_relevance: Opposite of compulsory — common in policy essays.

simple_definition: To gain or obtain something, especially through effort.
detailed_definition: To buy or obtain an object or asset for oneself; to learn or develop a skill or quality.
examples: Children acquire language skills remarkably quickly.
The company acquired a smaller competitor last year.
ielts_relevance: Common verb for describing learning and development.

simple_definition: To understand something fully.
detailed_definition: To grasp mentally; to understand fully.
examples: Young children may struggle to comprehend abstract concepts.
It's hard to comprehend the sheer scale of the disaster.
ielts_relevance: Formal synonym for 'understand' in academic writing.

simple_definition: To continue to have or keep something.
detailed_definition: To continue to have, hold, or keep something; to keep information in one's mind.
examples: Students often struggle to retain information learned through rote memorization.
The company managed to retain most of its customers during the crisis.
ielts_relevance: Common in education essays about memory and learning methods.

simple_definition: To understand something fully or firmly.
detailed_definition: To seize and hold firmly; to understand a difficult idea or subject fully.
examples: It took her a while to grasp the basic principles of economics.
He has a firm grasp of several foreign languages.
ielts_relevance: Useful informal-to-formal verb for describing understanding.

simple_definition: To encourage development or increased activity.
detailed_definition: To encourage an increase in activity, interest, or development; to arouse or spur on.
examples: Reading to young children helps stimulate their imagination.
Tax cuts are often used to stimulate economic growth.
ielts_relevance: Common verb for education and economy topics.

simple_definition: To give someone a reason or desire to do something.
detailed_definition: To provide someone with a motive or incentive to do something.
examples: Good teachers know how to motivate students who have lost interest.
Financial rewards alone may not be enough to motivate employees.
ielts_relevance: Extremely common verb in education and work essays.

simple_definition: To evaluate or estimate the nature or quality of something.
detailed_definition: To evaluate or estimate the nature, ability, or quality of something.
examples: Teachers use exams to assess students' understanding of the material.
It is difficult to assess the long-term impact of the policy.
ielts_relevance: Essential verb for discussing evaluation methods, especially education.

simple_definition: To judge or determine the value or quality of something.
detailed_definition: To form an idea of the amount, number, or value of something; to assess.
examples: It's important to evaluate all the available options before making a decision.
Employees are evaluated annually based on their performance.
ielts_relevance: Common academic verb useful across many essay types.

simple_definition: To clearly show that something exists or is true.
detailed_definition: To clearly show the existence or truth of something by giving proof or evidence.
examples: The study demonstrates a clear link between diet and heart disease.
She demonstrated great leadership during the crisis.
ielts_relevance: Common formal verb for presenting evidence in essays.

simple_definition: To explain or make clear by using examples.
detailed_definition: To explain or make something clear by using examples, charts, or pictures.
examples: The graph illustrates the sharp rise in unemployment during the recession.
Let me illustrate this point with a real-life example.
ielts_relevance: Extremely important for Task 1 essays describing charts/graphs.

simple_definition: To represent or show something in a picture or words.
detailed_definition: To represent or portray someone or something in a painting, drawing, or in words.
examples: The chart depicts the changes in global temperature over the last century.
The novel depicts life in a small rural village.
ielts_relevance: Useful synonym for 'show' in Task 1 introductions.

simple_definition: To point out or show something, often as a sign.
detailed_definition: To point out; to show or make known; to be a sign of something.
examples: The data indicates a steady decline in birth rates over the past decade.
Recent studies indicate a strong link between sleep and productivity.
ielts_relevance: One of the most common verbs for describing Task 1 data.

simple_definition: To reach a stable, level state after a period of change.
detailed_definition: To reach a state of little or no change after a period of activity or progress; to level off.
examples: Sales plateaued in the third quarter after two years of steady growth.
The number of new cases has plateaued in recent weeks.
ielts_relevance: High-value Task 1 verb for describing a flat trend after change.

simple_definition: To reach the highest point or value.
detailed_definition: To reach a maximum value, level, or degree.
examples: Tourist numbers typically peak during the summer months.
Unemployment peaked at over ten percent during the recession.
ielts_relevance: Fundamental Task 1 verb for describing the highest point on a graph.

simple_definition: To increase rapidly and to a high level.
detailed_definition: To rise rapidly to a high level or degree; to fly high in the air.
examples: Housing prices have soared in major cities over the last decade.
Demand for electric vehicles is expected to soar in coming years.
ielts_relevance: Strong Task 1 verb for a dramatic upward trend.

simple_definition: To stop rising or falling and become steady.
detailed_definition: To stop increasing or decreasing and remain at a steady level.
examples: After a period of rapid growth, the market began to level off.
Inflation is expected to level off by the end of the year.
ielts_relevance: Common Task 1 phrasal verb for describing stabilizing trends.

simple_definition: To go past and become greater or more successful.
detailed_definition: To surpass or become greater than another in number, importance, or value.
examples: China is expected to overtake the US as the world's largest economy.
Renewable energy usage overtook coal for the first time last year.
ielts_relevance: Common Task 1 verb for comparing two data series crossing.

simple_definition: To do or be better than someone or something else.
detailed_definition: To exceed or do better than a person, thing, or figure.
examples: The new smartphone's sales figures have surpassed all expectations.
Her performance in the exam surpassed everyone's expectations.
ielts_relevance: Formal synonym for 'overtake' or 'exceed' in Task 1 and 2.

simple_definition: A part or share of a whole, especially in relation to it.
detailed_definition: A part, share, or number considered in comparative relation to a whole.
examples: A large proportion of the population now lives in urban areas.
Only a small proportion of applicants are accepted each year.
ielts_relevance: Essential noun for Task 1 pie chart and percentage descriptions.

simple_definition: The greater number or part of something; more than half.
detailed_definition: The greater number or part of a group of people or things; more than half of a total.
examples: The majority of respondents said they were satisfied with the service.
A clear majority voted in favor of the new policy.
ielts_relevance: Essential quantifying noun for Task 1 and general essays.

simple_definition: The smaller part or number of a group; less than half.
detailed_definition: The smaller part or number, especially a group that differs from a larger group of which it is a part.
examples: Only a minority of employees chose to work from home full-time.
Ethnic minorities often face additional barriers to employment.
ielts_relevance: Opposite of majority — common in social essays and Task 1.

simple_definition: Numerical data collected and analyzed for information.
detailed_definition: A collection of numerical facts or data; the science of collecting and analyzing such data.
examples: According to recent statistics, crime rates have fallen in the city.
The statistics reveal a worrying trend in youth unemployment.
ielts_relevance: Common noun for referencing data sources in essays.

simple_definition: The result or consequence of an action or event.
detailed_definition: The way a thing turns out; a consequence or result.
examples: The outcome of the negotiations remains uncertain.
Regular exercise leads to better health outcomes overall.
ielts_relevance: Common noun for discussing results in Task 2 conclusions.

simple_definition: A likely consequence of something, often not directly stated.
detailed_definition: A conclusion that can be drawn from something although it is not explicitly stated; a likely consequence.
examples: The policy has serious implications for small businesses.
We must consider the long-term implications of this decision.
ielts_relevance: High-band noun for discussing indirect effects.

simple_definition: An unintended consequence, often negative, occurring some time later.
detailed_definition: An unintended consequence of an event or action, occurring some time afterward.
examples: The scandal had serious repercussions for the company's reputation.
Cutting funding for public transport could have negative repercussions on the environment.
ielts_relevance: High-band synonym for consequence, often negative.

simple_definition: A new plan or process to achieve a goal; the ability to act independently.
detailed_definition: A new plan or process to achieve something or solve a problem; the ability to assess and act independently.
examples: The government launched a new initiative to reduce plastic waste.
Employers value staff who show initiative rather than waiting for instructions.
ielts_relevance: Common noun for describing solutions and personal qualities.

simple_definition: To officially give resources for a particular purpose.
detailed_definition: To distribute resources or duties for a particular purpose.
examples: The government has allocated more funds to public healthcare this year.
Each team member was allocated a specific task for the project.
ielts_relevance: Common verb for essays about government spending or resource use.

simple_definition: To put money, time, or effort into something for future benefit.
detailed_definition: To put money, time, or effort into something with the expectation of achieving a profit or benefit.
examples: Governments should invest more heavily in public education.
She invested a great deal of time and effort into learning the language.
ielts_relevance: Common verb in essays about government spending and personal effort.

simple_definition: To control or maintain something through rules.
detailed_definition: To control an activity or process, especially through rules or laws.
examples: The industry is closely regulated to protect consumer rights.
Governments should regulate the use of harmful chemicals in food production.
ielts_relevance: Common verb for discussing government control in Task 2.

simple_definition: To make sure a law or rule is obeyed.
detailed_definition: To compel observance of or compliance with a law, rule, or obligation.
examples: Stricter penalties are needed to enforce traffic laws effectively.
The new dress code will be strictly enforced from next month.
ielts_relevance: Common verb for discussing rules and government policy.

simple_definition: A person who pays tax to the government.
detailed_definition: A person who pays a tax or is subject to taxation by a government.
examples: Critics argue that the project is a waste of taxpayers' money.
Taxpayers deserve to know exactly how their contributions are being spent.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about public spending and government responsibility.

simple_definition: Lacking basic necessities of life, such as food, money, or shelter.
detailed_definition: Suffering a severe and damaging lack of basic material and cultural benefits.
examples: Children from deprived backgrounds often struggle to access quality education.
The charity works in some of the most economically deprived areas of the country.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about poverty, inequality, and education access.

simple_definition: Having a great deal of wealth or money.
detailed_definition: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.
examples: Children from more affluent families often have access to better educational resources.
The neighborhood is known for being particularly affluent.
ielts_relevance: Opposite of 'deprived' — common in essays about inequality.

simple_definition: Money left after taxes that can be spent or saved freely.
detailed_definition: The income remaining after deduction of taxes, available for spending or saving.
examples: As disposable income rises, people tend to spend more on leisure activities.
Rising rents have significantly reduced young people's disposable income.
ielts_relevance: Common economics term for consumer spending essays.

simple_definition: The level of wealth and comfort available to a person or group.
detailed_definition: The degree of wealth and material comfort available to a person or community.
examples: Rapid economic growth has led to a marked improvement in the standard of living.
The standard of living varies greatly between urban and rural areas.
ielts_relevance: Extremely common phrase in economics and society essays.

simple_definition: The amount of money needed to cover basic expenses.
detailed_definition: The level of prices relating to a range of everyday items, especially as it affects a particular group.
examples: The rising cost of living has made it difficult for many families to make ends meet.
Big cities tend to have a much higher cost of living than rural towns.
ielts_relevance: Common economics phrase for essays about finances and cities.

simple_definition: To have just enough money to cover basic needs.
detailed_definition: To earn just enough money to live on or cover one's expenses.
examples: Many low-income families struggle to make ends meet each month.
With prices rising so fast, it's getting harder to make ends meet.
ielts_relevance: Common idiomatic phrase for Speaking Part 3 economics discussions.
